chunks: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ.
ai.seo_question: Why did God not make all people one community of believers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted not merely as a statement of divine will but as a justification for the natural diversity of creeds, distinguishing between the 'unity of essence' and the 'diversity of belief.' It underscores that human free will necessitates variation, making difference a permanent feature of earthly life rather than a defect to be eradicated by force. This perspective supports the Shia view that guidance is a divine gift, while the manifestation of belief is subject to human choice and historical context.
